children: The state government links the move to engineers’ contribution to technological development and economic progress

The Karnataka government has declared 15 September as Engineers’ Day and permitted engineers in the state to use the prefix ‘Er.’ before their names, recognising their contribution to technological development and economic progress. The government order was issued on 15 September, the birth anniversary of engineer and former Diwan of Mysore Sir M Visvesvaraya, following an announcement by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar.

The government said the decision was intended to formally recognise the contribution of engineers to society and the development of the country. The order also permits engineers across Karnataka to use ‘Er.’ before their names as a distinctive professional title.
The government has said September 15 will be observed as Engineers’ Day in honour of Visvesvaraya, who was born in Muddenahalli, Karnataka, in 1861.

The order highlighted his contribution to infrastructure and institution building during his tenure as the 19th Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1918. It cited projects and institutions associated with his work, including the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) Dam, Bhadravati Iron and Steel Works, Mysore Sandalwood Oil Factory, Mysore Soap Factory, University of Mysore and State Bank of Mysore.

Shivakumar said the state produces more than one lakh engineers each year and that recognising their contribution was the government’s responsibility. He also said the role of engineers had expanded beyond traditional areas such as architecture and construction to sectors including energy, infrastructure and information technology.

The Chief Minister said the state would officially celebrate Engineers’ Day from next year. He made the announcement after paying tribute to Visvesvaraya at his statue. The government’s decision comes shortly after Karnataka allowed teachers to use the prefix ‘Tr’ before their names. The state had announced the measure on 5 September as a mark of recognition for teachers’ contribution to society.

The Karnataka government’s order describes the ‘Er.’ prefix as a symbol of engineers’ professional contribution and lifelong service. Engineers across the state may use the prefix before their names under the new order.
